summary: Built 1936 on the Tonto NF as a Region 3 L-4 variant; NRHP-listed 1988 and NHLR-registered 2002; latest staffing record is a 2013 visit.

facts.design: Region 3 variant of the L-4; 30-ft tower with 12x12 cab (sources describe the tower differently: Pacific Coast Steel vs MC-24)

events.note: Built on the Tonto National Forest as a Region 3 variant of the L-4

Listed as Diamond Point Lookout Cabin, NRIS 87002493
Dude Fire burned the Zane Grey cabin in the vicinity of the lookout; six firefighters died in the fire
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on July 20, 2002
Visit report dated September 17, 2013 answered yes to staffed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia's category tags say Coronado National Forest and Santa Cruz County, but its infobox, the NHLR page and the NRIS record say Tonto National Forest and Gila County. The Gila County reading is used.

notes_for_editor: Build year 1936 is solid across three sources. Staffing rests only on a 2013 visit report, so current staffing is unknown. Current access, rental and climbability were not found in the pages read. Tower description conflicts: NHLR credits Pacific Coast Steel, while Forest Lookouts gives an MC-24 tower with no maker named. A peakbagging.com search snippet gives 6380 ft; NHLR and Wikipedia give 6157 ft (1,877 m), matching the brief, so the snippet was not used. The Dude Fire burned the Zane Grey cabin, not the lookout; the events list keeps that distinction.
